lis.profile: Lis — a cool, deadpan, ironic street narrator of an adult comedy show about used-car flippers and scams. Low calm voice, dry humor, confident.
lis.notes: Each line is separate, with a clear 0.8-second pause between lines. You narrate a dark-humor comedy about how fast resellers call a grandma who listed her car. Deadpan, dry punchlines after a tiny pause, perfect comic timing. «БМВ» say as «бэ-эм-вэ».

seryoga.profile: Seryoga — a naive, kind young Russian guy in his 20s who buys a used car; eager, a bit gullible, but learns fast. Bright, quick voice.
seryoga.notes: One line: hopeful, cheerful, a bit too late.

vika.profile: Vika — a sharp, confident young Russian woman in her 20s, street-smart, ironic, protective friend. Clear, firm voice with a smirk.
vika.notes: Each line is separate, with a clear 1-second pause between lines. Line 1: loud, firm, to a minibus driver. Line 2: polite, confident, businesslike.

mihalych.profile: Mihalych — an old, experienced Russian car mechanic in his 60s, gruff, calm, a bit tired, speaks like a master who has seen everything. Low husky voice.
mihalych.notes: One line: old honest master looking at an engine, tired dry humor, unhurried; the last sentence is a deadpan punchline.

tolyan.profile: Tolyan — a cocky Russian used-car flipper (perekup) in his 30s, street swagger, deep raspy voice, show-off, calls everyone "брат". Adult street comedy, not for kids.
tolyan.notes: Each line is separate, with a clear 1-second pause between lines. Line 1: excited command, like a trader on a stock floor. Line 2: fast, pushy phone pitch. Line 3: smug, quick. Line 4: shouting up from a ladder to a window. Line 5: bitter, annoyed.

galya.profile: Baba Galya — a kind, sharp-tongued Russian grandmother in her 70s selling her old BMW; warm folksy voice, calls everyone «сынок» and «милок», slightly cracked old voice, unimpressed by hustlers.
galya.notes: Each line is separate, with a clear 1-second pause between lines. Line 1: naive, unhurried. Line 2: puzzled. Line 3: ironic, into the phone. Line 4: delighted, approving. Line 5: sweet but merciless punchline.

edik.profile: Edik — a slick, fast-talking Russian car dealership manager in his 30s, overly polite, pushy, fake-friendly smile in the voice, sales script energy.
edik.notes: One line on the phone: slick, fast, defensive, overly cheerful, trying to calm her down.

inspector.profile: A tired Russian traffic police registration clerk, a woman in her 40s, bureaucratic, flat, indifferent voice, has seen everything.
inspector.notes: One line, flat and indifferent, reading from a monitor; the last words are said dryly, without any emotion.

seller.profile: A cheerful man from Vladivostok selling his lowered Toyota from a balcony, loud, friendly, joking, a bit of a hustler.
seller.notes: One line, shouted happily from a balcony, joking.

dps.profile: A calm, tired Russian traffic police officer at a night checkpoint, short and formal.
dps.notes: One line, two short sentences, flat and formal. Pronounce «ОСАГО» clearly as a separate word: о-са-го.

razbor.profile: A fast-talking Russian junkyard parts seller in his 40s, hoarse, cheerful, a hustler, sells used engines.
razbor.notes: One line, loud and quick sales pitch; the last phrase is a cheeky joke said fast.

pristav.profile: A calm, formal Russian court bailiff in his 40s, polite, bureaucratic, unhurried.
pristav.notes: Each line is separate, with a clear 1-second pause between lines. Line 1: formal, reading from a paper. Line 2: short dry deadpan reply.

banker.profile: A polite, cold Russian bank manager woman in her 30s, corporate smile in the voice.
banker.notes: One line, polite and cold; the last two words are a deadpan corporate punchline.

master.profile: A gruff Russian underground garage craftsman, low hoarse voice, works with a hammer, few words.
master.notes: Each line is separate, with a clear 1-second pause between lines. Short, gruff, businesslike.

expert.profile: A meticulous Russian forensic vehicle expert in his 50s, calm, precise, a little bored, nerdy.
expert.notes: One line: calm, precise, matter-of-fact; the last sentence is a dry nerdy punchline. Say «VIN» as «вин».

sled.profile: A tired Russian police investigator in his 40s, flat, ironic, has seen everything.
sled.notes: One line: flat, ironic; the last two words are a deadpan punchline after a tiny pause.
